cues.show: Your face close up, doing a lip roll with no sound from the tool.
cues.say: This is a lip roll. Your lips are loose and closed, and the air makes them buzz, like a child playing with a toy car.

cues.show: Close up: a finger on each cheek, lip roll again.
cues.say: If your lips stop, put a finger on each cheek and lift a little. Keep the breath steady and gentle.

cues.show: The lip roll tool on screen. Point at the line and where your line will be drawn.
cues.say: The tool plays a soft tone that slides through your voice, and draws its path as a line. The microphone draws your line over it.

cues.show: Press Start and do two rounds.
cues.say: Press Start below. The microphone starts with it.

cues.show: Press Start and do two rounds.
cues.say: First the tone plays, then you lip roll the same slide by yourself.

cues.show: Point at your line wandering around the tool's line.
cues.say: Your line doesn't have to sit exactly on the tool's line. An easy, steady buzz matters more than the exact note.

cues.show: Point at your line wandering around the tool's line.
cues.say: _Keep it quiet: a lip roll should never feel like pushing._

cues.show: Point at your line wandering around the tool's line.
cues.say: Practice until the buzz stays even through the whole slide.

cues.show: Open the settings button: Tone, then Speed. Do a lip roll on a tune you know.
cues.say: Try things with it. The settings button has Tone, where you can roll along with the tone or with no tone at all, and Speed.

cues.show: Open the settings button: Tone, then Speed. Do a lip roll on a tune you know.
cues.say: Away from the tool, lip roll a tune you know well.

cues.show: Open the settings button: Tone, then Speed. Do a lip roll on a tune you know.
cues.say: Slide from as low as is easy to as high as is easy, then back, on one breath.
